Rationale: The fly meaning is exact and the source supplies Munda *roj/*roko, but Nihali eḍ(u)go requires several unexplained segment changes.
Nihali lāŋg and Proto-Munda *laŋ 'tongue' are near-identical; this strongly supports contact but does not distinguish borrowing from inheritance.
Nihali avar and Proto-Kherwarian *ɔɽaʔ 'house' share a plausible vowel-liquid frame, but the direction and regularity are not established.
Nihali mindi 'night' and Proto-Munda *juʔp have neither close form nor a proposed recurring correspondence.
Nihali biʈil and Proto-Kherwarian *gitil 'sand' are near-identical apart from the initial consonant; this is strong contact evidence.
The shared rot meaning is relevant, but saratin versus *sɔɛa is formally distant and lacks a worked phonological derivation.

Nihali ṭivi 'to carry in hand' plausibly contains Proto-Munda *tiiʔ 'hand', but *tiiʔ is a body-part noun rather than the full carry verb and the Nihali -vi material is not analyzed; contact is plausible, while inheritance is unproven.
Nihali batāme and Proto-Kherwarian *tɛtaŋ share the thirst meaning, but the initial and final correspondences are not independently established.
Nihali sāli 'bark/skin' and Proto-Munda *usal may involve metathesis, but the closer Korku and Indo-Aryan forms make this Munda parent non-unique.
Nihali robān and Proto-Kherwarian *rabaŋ 'cold' are close and likely represent contact; Korku mediation remains possible.
Nihali pala 'leaf' and Proto-Munda *vla are moderately close, but the p~v relation needs a larger series.
Nihali cokob and Proto-Kherwarian *sakam 'leaf' are distant overall but contribute one instance of the recurring initial c~s proposal.
Nihali bakán and Proto-Kherwarian *bagi share the leave/release meaning and an initial ba- frame, though the medial and final development is not regularized.
Nihali osonkamā-be 'boil' and Proto-Munda *v₂₃sin are formally remote and no recurring derivation is supplied.
Nihali bāba and Proto-Munda *baaʔ 'paddy' are near-identical and provide strong contact evidence.
Nihali jumu 'name' and Proto-Munda *ɲv₃₃m are too distant under the current transcription to support a correspondence without further analysis.

Nihali cana- and Proto-Kherwarian *susun 'dance' share meaning and a possible initial c~s relation, but the remaining segments are not close; this parent is also used by another Nihali citation cluster.
Nihali tʰyén and Proto-Kherwarian tahɛ-n 'stay' are close in form and meaning, favoring contact.
Nihali apʰír and Proto-Kherwarian *apir 'fly' are near-identical; this is strong contact evidence, not a diagnostic sound law.
Nihali bigi 'blow' and Proto-Munda *peʔt share meaning but have only a possible initial voicing relation and no close remainder.
Nihali kúlā and Proto-Munda *kəla 'tiger' are close in form and exact in meaning.
Nihali lāñ and Proto-Munda *laŋ 'tongue' are effectively identical under transcriptional normalization; this duplicates the same parent represented by lāŋg.
Nihali cʰāga and Proto-Kherwarian *sagaʔ denote the same grass and closely match apart from the proposed initial c~s relation.
Nihali biṭini 'bed/spread bedclothes' and Proto-Munda *bel are semantically related but formally incomplete and lack a recurring medial derivation.
Nihali cana-be and Proto-Kherwarian *susun 'dance' repeat the same c~s proposal and the same parent as cana-, so this is not an independent correspondence set.
Nihali samma-(ki) 'front' and Proto-Munda *sv₂maŋ share the s-m frame and meaning, but intervening material remains unexplained.
Nihali aphirka and Proto-Kherwarian *apir 'fly' are near-identical after stripping citation morphology; this repeats the same parent as apʰír.
Nihali petek and Proto-Kherwarian *pɛʈɛɟ 'break' are near-identical under broad transcriptional normalization.

Nihali bãe(n) 'spread leaves on a roof; thatch' closely matches Juang bɛn under Proto-Munda *bel 'spread (vt)' in both form and verbal meaning; this corrects the false English leaves/leave semantic bridge to Proto-Kherwarian *bagi 'leave'.
Nihali samma kʰuri 'front leg' repeats the samma~*sv₂maŋ comparison and therefore does not add an independent root.
Nihali mungukā 'dirty' and Proto-Munda *kum... are formally remote and would require unmotivated metathesis and segment loss.
Nihali cʰondevo and Proto-Kherwarian *sɔndɔrɔ 'pus' share a substantial medial frame and add a non-identical c~s instance.
Nihali kubāy 'heavy/improve in health' and Proto-Kherwarian *hamal are both formally and semantically loose.
